question.problem: Find the position vector of $A( -1,2 )$ in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}.$
question.worked_solution:
Our vector is shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252323/assets/269326f4375dfad6d05e4468f4831012bde4a57bc85fbdfc7082cc466d3522dd.png)

Remember that in general, if a point $A$ has coordinates $(a_x,a_y),$ then its position vector is given by

$$
\overrightarrow{OA} = a_x\mathbf{i}+a_y\mathbf{j}.
$$

Here, the point $A$ has coordinates $(-1,2),$ so its position vector is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OA} & =(-1)\cdot i+2\cdot j \\  & =-i+2j.\end{aligned}
$$
